messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: high-severity incident detected on streaming-decode pool — multiple CUDA OOMs and container restarts, impact: some customer requests dropped. auto-escalation to #incidents.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0178, paging oncall (emily) for decode node flapping + OOMs. Logs attached to the incident.

emily: saw the pager. I'm looking at the streamer logs now. initial symptom: sudden memory spike on decode pods, repeated `cudaErrorOutOfMemory` and processes being killed by k8s.

raj: are these coming from a single model/version or widespread? any header bypass / max_tokens anomalies?

emily: early signs point to a subset of tenants hitting runaway generations. There's a mismatch between client-side max_tokens and the enforcement layer on the edge. some requests had `max_tokens: 1e6` (buggy SDK).

lucy: :eyes: confirmed. I traced one trace id — client sent an invalid header `x-client-max-tokens: 1000000`. edge rejected it but our old proxy forwarded to runtime with default fallback, which allowed long decode to continue.

mike: noted. while we triage, we should protect capacity: 1) throttle decode requests from the pool, 2) enable emergency token ceiling on the cluster, 3) route traffic to a lighter quantized model variant. who can flip the ceiling?

emily: I can flip a cluster-wide cap for streaming to 2048 tokens. doing it now via deploy console.

emily: done — global_streaming_token_ceiling = 2048 applied. watching memory.

raj: I'll push a temporary routing rule: for requests > 512 tokens route to quant-rtx fallback. Applying now.

lucy: applied route. Also adding an NGINX quick fix: reject requests with `x-client-max-tokens` > 10000 at the edge. patching config and reloading.

sre-bridge-bot: bridge created: zoom.us/j/123456789 — oncall + infra + platform in bridge.

ce-support: customer impact — Support ticket #C-8123 shows 37 customers with 4xx/5xx during the window. top affected customer: Acme Analytics (region us-west). Escalated to CS, sending a DM to account lead.

emily: memory pressure dropping after caps and routing. node restarts reduced. seeing some residual `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` on one node — isolating that node for a reboot.

mike: I'll cordon the node (gpunode-14) and drain. also increasing eviction grace to avoid thrashing.

lucy: quick log snippet that caused OOM (redacted):

```
# request id: r-9f4c
headers: {"x-client-max-tokens": "1000000", "model": "gpt-decode-v2"}
trace: decode loop allocated KV cache growth ~1.2GB/s
panic: cudaErrorOutOfMemory at decode step 3121
```

raj: thanks. this is definitely runaway generation. Looks like some SDK versions silently send huge token caps when user uses streaming + bad `max_tokens` handling. we should block at edge and add runtime sanity checks.

emily: agreed. action items for immediate remediation: 1) edge block (done), 2) cluster token ceiling (done), 3) route long requests to quant fallback (done), 4) cordon faulty node (in progress).

ce-support: customers on ticket are being notified: "We're mitigating a streaming issue causing request drops; applying temporary limits; no data loss expected. We'll follow up with timeline."

sre-bridge-bot: oncall-handoff reminder in 20 mins to secondary (raj).

lucy: also enabled a request-sampling hook for bad requests so we can capture offending headers and traces for postmortem (sampling rate 1/10 for >1024 tokens).

mike: node gpunode-14 drained and rebooting. if reboot doesn't clear `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`, we'll mark it for hardware validation.

emily: memory usage steady, OOMs stopped in last 2 mins. requests returning 200 more consistently. throttling has reduced overall throughput by ~18% for affected customers — we'll call this acceptable short-term.

raj: moving to followup/next steps: 1) patch SDK validation to not allow >100k tokens in header, 2) runtime: enforce per-request max token sanity (hardcap 50k), 3) add automated fallback when decode time per token exceeds threshold (indicates runaway), 4) update runbooks to include edge header checks.

emily: I'll open a reticket for infra to run hardware checks on gpunode-14 and add a post-restart validation job.

ce-support: CS will prepare customer-facing timeline and a short RCA once we have root cause. priority to Acme Analytics and any paying customers impacted.

sre-bridge-bot: Incident update posted to INC-2026-0178: mitigations applied, partial customer impact, oncall continuing monitoring for 60 minutes.

mike: during the mitigation we also applied an emergency rollback of a decode performance change that inadvertently removed a token cap check earlier — rolling that back prevented a recurrence.

lucy: small note: we saw 3 containers hit OOMs but only one node required reboot. remaining pods recovered via restart policy.

emily: preparing to handoff to raj in 18 mins. summary for handoff: cause - client-sent oversized token header + missing runtime sanity check; impact - ~37 customers saw request drops, top affected acme, mitigations - edge block, cluster token ceiling, routing to quant fallback, node reboot; next steps - SDK/runtime patches, hardware validation, customer communication.

raj: thanks. I'll take over monitoring and drive the SDK/runtime tickets. please push any traces and the sampled payload set to INC-2026-0178 artifacts.

ce-support: file notes: impacted window 2026-03-15T18:12:30Z -> 2026-03-15T18:38:19Z, estimated dropped requests ~4200, severity: high, revenue impact: under review.

emily: handing off now — logged everything in incident doc. ping me if it flares. :white_check_mark:

raj: taking it from here. closing bridge in 10. we'll do a full postmortem and include a checklist for token caps and edge validation.

sre-bridge-bot: bridge closed. incident remains open for postmortem and follow-ups.
